the rewrite finds store 1 by the signed low byte of its offset (p = buf + (signed char)buf[2], cbw R035+0x1615 after the load at R035+0x15A2): with store 1 at 0x80 or later (a table of 128 bytes or more, the 198-byte one of a game's file too) the other stores are copied from the wrong bytes; and it reopens the file without truncating it (R035+0x15DD, mode 1), so bytes left after a shrunk store stay and a store appended after them is later copied into an earlier one. the formula's risk works backwards: the explosion (longer = 1, the inn barred 120 days) comes when rand_mod(4 - risk) is not 0, so a low-risk formula (0) explodes three times in four and a high-risk one (2) half the time.
boosts given to the whole party are never taken back (FixEverybodyBoostsUndone).

the weapon potions' kind 0x4A events (Deadly Blade, Strongedge, Great Power: PotionEffects.Drink) run out here and nothing is undone: only kinds 0x48 and 0x49 are, so the bonus byte (+0x34) keeps them for good.

the recorded amount is taken off whatever the attribute is by then (add_attr(owner, type, -value)): a boost that a night's rest (Endurance back to its maximum) or wounds (Strength) have already used up is taken off again and leaves the attribute below where it was; a saint's lowering (a negative value) is given back the same way.

the table comes back compacted, and what a battle put into the slots below the count is lost: a saint's boost (kind 0x48/0x49) or a price called in a battle is never undone, as its event, which would end it, is gone.

"forever" events end on 31 December 1499: 9999 hours is the fixed end 23:00 31.12.1499, not an open end, so on 1 January 1500 every such event expires (a quest clears its facts) and one created later expires at the next expiry pass; the witches' sabbat quest and its planned sabbat end for good.
the new event already holds the value before the op (FixNewEventAddDoubles).

asking for kind 0x1C (location facts) also returns the kind 8 events (R029+0x3279..0x3281: `cmp cx,0x1c`, `cmp ax,8`): every fact scan (loc_fact, loc_fact_value and the like) sees the quests. A city's politics quest (type 0, value = the city's number) answers "fact 0" of that city, which should be the leaning.

the icon loop's bounds are one row and one column too wide: an icon in column col + 18 is written at G[y - tope][19], which is G[y - tope + 1][0] (the next row's first cell, over its terrain, or past the buffer for the last row), and one in row tope + 50 at G[50][..], the bytes after the buffer, which no fill clears. Reproduced (the camp watch and the party drawing's masks read both).

the block is read through the buffer's flat layout with no bounds check (R030+0x261D..0x2639): a column past 18 is the next row's cell (col + i - 19 of row + j + 1: the west side of the window, one row down) and a row past 49 is the bytes after the buffer (zeros and the stale icons of Fill, then the party icon table). The marker's column is up to 16 and its row up to 47, so up to 9 columns wrap and up to 7 rows fall past the buffer. Reproduced: a settlement there changes the bonus; one in the true cells beyond is not seen.

scrolling up moves d slots, not 0x83 - d: slots 2d .. 0x82 keep the rows they held, d rows further down the map than their new place. With the scroll's d = 0x41 only slot 0x82 is stale; when the buffer's top is clamped to row 0 (old top 0x18 or 0x30 from overland_open, d = old) the rows from slot 2d on are 0x18 / 0x30 rows off until the next scroll down reads them again. Reproduced: the map drawing (and the cell reads of the step and the camp) show those rows (checked by direct calls of 1dd4 in the original).

the whole charm byte but bit 7 counts as armour: its high nibble (bits 4-6) is the fire charm that Firewall (+1 each), St.Polycarp, St.Charity and the other SetCharm saints set, so they give +16 to +112 armour that never wears off (the "invulnerable after Polycarp and Firewall" bug); only the low nibble is the potions' and saints' armour.

the weapon potions' bonus byte counts with any weapon the member strikes with (bows and fists too), where the manual and the potions' own descriptions limit Deadly Blade, Strongedge and Great Power to some kinds of weapon.
the penetration wraps: (bonus + weapon) & 15, so Strongedge or Great Power on a weapon of high penetration gives almost none ("after Great Power my bows only do 3-5 damage").

damage queued faster than it is applied (blows resolved at engagement time, applied at the end of each attacker's animation; traps) wraps past 127 to a negative queue, which damage_apply's signed test (jle 42) lets through: the target gains Endurance (and Strength, for the second byte) instead of losing it.

OriginalBehaviour.FixLootExitTestReadsWords - the test reads cbt_floor (a byte table, DS:A6B4) as words at 2 x slot: it skips slot s only when combatant 2s's floor is -99 (0x9D) and combatant 2s + 1's is -1 (0xFF), so a member who left is not skipped (direct calls of R040+0x0C22 from the battle state street-p100 with key D and DS:8DC4 = 0: member 1's floor byte 0x9D gives DS:8DC4 = 1 without the message; floor bytes 2, 3 = 0x9D, 0xFF give DS:8DC4 = 2 after R022+0x04E4); tests: BattleEndTests

the missile skill is the readied weapon's at the battle's end: a member who threw his last javelin or axe has weapon -1 (use_ammo), whose category byte (R136+0x75AB, before the table) is 0, so Edged is practised instead of the thrown weapon's skill, beside the hand weapon's own (flail, spear ...).
the original removes an empty group by shifting the later groups down but keeps testing the same (stale, zero) counter, so every group after the first empty one is removed too.

the record's +0x00 word is the roster's location of the character and the combatant's scrx: the battle's last frame leaves the member's screen x there (cbt_screen_pos R014+0x99F6), which the inn's roster later reads as a location.

the original draws until the room differs from the gate room, which never happens when the only room it can draw is the gate room (the game then freezes; the emulated original does not return for seed 49955, lore 3, cleared 28, specs (46,4,2) (60,6,8) (41,5,3)).

a corridor's decoration spot can fall past its end: it is counted from the far end (o1, and o3 below) rather than from o0 (o2), so only a roll of 1 falls on the corridor; larger rolls test, and may mark, the cells past its end.
the fortress relics are forced to quality 35: the three relics get quality 0x23 and type 0x9F whatever DARKLAND.LST gives them (the relic weapons have qualities 50..85 and weapon types).
loot counts wrap at 255: the counts are added in a byte with no limit test, so equal items totalling more than 255 wrap and the excess is lost.

R014+0x48CA leaves through the common exit (R014+0x4B36): R014+0x4B5A (for an enemy) puts every door that is no twin back to the open flags DS:E0C0 kept at the last enemy search that opened them, though this search opened none, and copies those flags back (DS:E0C0 to the level's +0x33D3): a door opened or shut since then is set back.

a path of fewer than 2 steps (a lead whose first step meets its target gives the bare 0xFF) is read before its start: the previous combatant's path bytes 248, 249 (for combatant 0 the last loot pile record's +10, +11, 20A5:6236, which no code writes: 0 here).

OriginalBehaviour.FixStairsKeyWithoutSelection - R016+0x0165..0x0169 copies entry [DS:A6B2] of the two member tables without testing it: with nobody selected (0xFF) entry -1, DS:C77D = DS:C8B1 (the bytes before the tables).

OriginalBehaviour.FixStairsWallMarkLost - the write below goes to the level's buffer, and level_switch (R024+0x05B4, called at R023+0x16C7) saves the level it leaves only when DS:D4E4 is set (LevelChanged: any change of the level sets it; level_switch and the battle's end R014+0x069A clear it), which this write does not do: after a switch with DS:D4E4 clear the original reloads the old level without the 0xFF (the levels stay in memory here, the mark is taken back by SaveLevelOrLoseUnsaved).
items are consumed until none of that type and quality is left: the spares stacked with the worn piece (worn down with it by WearItem) are thrown away with it.
armour wear hits the whole stack: the stack loses the quality, not one piece, so identical spare pieces stacked with the worn armour wear down with it.
the loop runs to the count inclusive, so the slot after the last cloud (an old cloud's copy, or zeros) is tested too (OriginalBehaviour.FixCloudLineOneTooMany stops at the last cloud).
a missed box reloads the line from the saved words, which are the stack residue until a box was hit: the clouds after it are tested against that line (3, 17405)-(state words), not a → t. Kept.

the loop sets only the line's end (DS:E0A9/E0A7, R018+0x09D5/0x09DC) and relies on its start (DS:E0A5/E0A3, set to the caster at R018+0x0851); the area test it calls for the enemies (R014+0x469E, 0E76:469E) writes the start itself, from its first instruction on (0E76:46E5/46EC: the centre = the member), so after a member's count the next member's line starts at the previous member, not at the caster. Kept (found by f2witch2f: a member behind a wall counted as seen, the target chosen differed).
OriginalBehaviour.FixEscapeWithoutSelectionPauseByte - flags[-1]'s high byte is the pause byte DS:A695 (R016+0x15BE, bx = -2)

OriginalBehaviour.FixLeaveOrderModeWithoutSelection - Enter travelling individually (R016+0x0734) calls it with nobody selected, and a cursor target left by the button held over a member (R014+0xB632..: the target of that member's order) gives the order to record -1: for 0x400 the pause byte loses 0x10; the 0x1BE test clears it too; a missile (0x80) sets 0x02 of the pause byte; a missile or a throw sets exchange[12] = 7 (Ready) and repath[12] = the order clock DS:C867; an attack with bit 1 (or adjacent) sets exchange[12] = 7; a walk to a spot sets exchange[12] = 0 and give-up[12] = the order clock + 30, or, the party split in real combat, shows "USE STAIRS..." (DS:064A) for 150 ticks.

OriginalBehaviour.FixEscapeWithoutSelectionPauseByte - with nobody selected the xor at R016+0x13F9 (bx = -2) lands on flags[-1]'s high byte, the pause byte DS:A695: its bit 0x10 becomes DS:D6EA (the flee bit before order mode), so a pause byte of 1 with D6EA = 1 turns 0x11, which the tests for paused (== 1) and for running (== 0) both refuse.

DS:9084 (Battle.LeaveAfterVictory, set when an enemy that ends the battle dies) is not among what is written (R003 never touches it): a castle battle saved after its lord fell and loaded again does not end with the victory, and leaving counts as fleeing.
OriginalBehaviour.FixSaveWriterSkipsEmptySlots - R037+0x2ACE leaves the record out and writes the full count, so the file is short and the original's loader reads out of step.

OriginalBehaviour.FixSaveWriterSkipsEmptySlots - the same for a slot past party_size: the writer tests all five ids, and a slot past party_size has status 0 (party_size is one past the last slot of status != 0), so its record is left out as well.
OriginalBehaviour.FixLoadScreenEscape - Esc on the load screen goes on with the emptied slots and no events.
party_delete_vec runs while the events are in events.tmp, so a member who died in the battle keeps the term and "has left" events (kinds 0x43/0x47) it would cancel: they come back with the table.

R030+0x1133..0x1154 sets DS:286E to the last 0x83 rows without reading them (no call of R030+0x1DD4 on this path): when the buffer's top was not already there (a top of 0x318 from overland_open, the party walking south), the row buffer keeps the rows from the old top and the map drawn (and the cells read) from it are (height - 0x83 - old top) rows north of the view's registers until a scroll reads the rows again. Reproduced (map.Rows is left as it is).
